title: introduce-route-rollups-and-attribution-indexing-for-observability
author: Marco Nguyen
description:
Motivation: Current observability surfaces provide detailed per-request token cost and latency, but we lack a scalable, route-oriented rollup and an efficient way to correlate sampled KV-cache traces back to route-level cost attribution. This PR implements route rollups for token-level metrics, a lightweight attribution index that ties sampled KV/tracer spans to route keys, and a set of Grafana panels and alert rule improvements to reduce noisy alerts on long-tail routes.

Design summary: 
- Prometheus metric rollups: add prometheus metrics with suffixed _route_rollup that aggregate token_count, token_cost_usd, and tail_latency_ms by route and time window. Rollups are emitted at the collector sidecar and computed with series cardinality controls (hashed route buckets + tag cardinality caps).
- Attribution index: introduce an append-only, sharded in-memory index (observability/attribution_index) that stores a compact mapping from sampled trace_id -> {route_bucket, token_window_hash}. Span enrichment adds an index lookup id to tracer spans so sampled KV-cache traces can be resolved to route rollups without scanning logs. The index is ephemeral and bounded by memory and TTL to preserve privacy and performance.
- Tracing changes: add a small span attribute `obs.route_bucket` and `obs.attribution_id` for sampled KV/kv-cache spans. OTEL exporter includes these attributes and a small indexer process batches them to the attribution index.
- Dashboards & alerts: new Grafana dashboard `Route Rollups` with top-N route cost/latency panels, 95/99 percentile time-series per route bucket, and a heatmap for route cost concentration. Prometheus alert rules tuned to use percentile-based thresholds per route_bucket instead of a single global SLO, and with a noise suppression window for routes under 100 requests/min.

Backward compatibility and migration: instrumentation changes are additive. Rollups are opt-in via feature flag `obs.route_rollups.enabled` (off by default); tracing attributes are guarded by `obs.attribution.tracing` (default on for sampled traces). The attribution index runs in the observability sidecar by default but can be disabled for Private installs to avoid memory overhead.

Performance and safety: rollups reduce cardinality by hashing route names into 256 buckets by default; this value is configurable. Attribution index uses a fixed-size ring buffer per shard with LRU eviction to prevent unbounded growth. Benchmarks included show <2% CPU overhead on a 1000rps mixed workload with sampling_rate=0.02.

Files changed: Collector sidecar rollup emitter, OTEL span enricher, attribution index implementation, Grafana JSON dashboard, Prometheus alert rules, docs and migration notes, e2e tests and a small perf benchmark harness.

Checklist: 
- [x] Add collector-side rollup emitter
- [x] Add attribution index and span enrichment
- [x] Add Grafana dashboard and alert tuning
- [x] Add unit tests for index eviction behavior
- [x] Add e2e test that validates attribution lookup for sampled traces
- [x] Add migration docs and feature flags

Impact: When enabled, product teams will see aggregated per-route cost/latency insights with reduced cardinality, and SRE will be able to configure per-route alerts based on percentiles. Short-term risk: potential alerting blind spots if teams forget to enable rollups for newly added routes; mitigated by a dashboard flag that highlights routes without rollup coverage.

Notes: This PR intentionally keeps attribution metadata minimal to avoid PII leakage. The attribution_id is a salted hash and the index TTL defaults to 5 minutes. Ops can tune both via config. For Private deployments, ops can disable the attribution index or reduce sampling.

References: Linear ENG-7421, ENG-7540 for requirements; internal perf benchmark results attached in commits.

review_comments: Aisha Kaur (2026-02-16): Can we limit the default bucket count to 128 instead of 256? Marco: I ran perf with both; 256 reduces false positives on hot route fragmentation. Added config to make it tunable.

Diego Morales (2026-02-17): The attribution index eviction policy needs clearer invariants around TTL vs LRU. Marco: added unit tests and expanded comments in index.go; eviction uses TTL first then LRU within the TTL window.

Priya Patel (2026-02-18): Alert rule for tail_latency should include a suppression window for <100rpm routes. Marco: implemented suppression and added a dashboard panel that highlights suppressed routes.
Aisha Kaur (2026-02-19): Minor nits on PromQL in route_alerts.yaml. Marco: fixed and squashed into branch.
Diego Morales (2026-02-19): Approved after tests green.

release_notes: Add optional route rollups for token-level cost and latency; introduce a lightweight attribution index to correlate sampled KV-cache traces with route buckets; new Grafana Route Rollups dashboard and tuned per-route percentile alerts. Feature is behind configs obs.route_rollups.enabled and obs.attribution.tracing.
